paragraphs: Hammersmith and Fulham Council runs its fostering service jointly with the Royal Borough of Kensington and Chelsea and Westminster City Council. Enquiries from people interested in fostering go through Foster with West London, the shared recruitment service for eight west London councils: Brent, Ealing, Hammersmith and Fulham, Harrow, Hillingdon, Hounslow, Kensington and Chelsea, and Westminster. In May 2025 the council said the biggest challenge was that there are not enough foster carers in west London, with more than 700 needed across the area.

The council welcomes applications for long-term and short-term fostering from people of all backgrounds. When you get in touch, an enquiry officer usually phones you to explain the requirements and the assessment, which the council describes as taking about six months, and then passes your details to the council you choose within the partnership. The council says carers can work flexibly around fostering, and one local carer featured by the council chose to look after children aged 12 and over so that fostering fitted around her job.

Approved carers have their own social worker and the backing of the borough's fostering team. Hammersmith and Fulham also exempts its foster carers from council tax, a change it highlighted in early 2024. The council's fostering page does not publish allowance rates, so ask for the current figures when you speak to the team.

The council holds monthly information sessions where you can find out more before you apply. Speak to Foster with West London and to two or three of the agencies shown above, and compare the training, out-of-hours support and payments each offers before you decide.
